Title: Dress code: White tie – what to wear
Description: The most formal dress code there is, for state banquets, grand balls and royal occasions. Men: Black tailcoat, stiff white wing-collar shirt, white bow tie, white piqué waistcoat, black patent shoes. Decorations if applicable. Women: Floor-length evening gown, often with long gloves. Shoulders covered at official occasions.

Women: Floor-length evening gown, or a very elegant cocktail dress. Jewellery and a clutch.

Title: Dress code: Cocktail – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Glam – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Elegant casual – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Parisian chic – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Business formal – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Business casual – what to wear
Description: Professional without suit and tie. The default in many offices. Men: Chinos or trousers, shirt or polo, optional blazer; no tie. Loafers or smart sneakers. Women: Trousers or skirt with blouse or fine knit, optional blazer; smart flats or low heels.

Title: Dress code: Smart casual – what to wear
Description: Polished but relaxed. One of the most common (and confusing) codes. Men: Dark jeans or chinos, shirt or fine knit, optional blazer, smart sneakers or loafers. No tracksuits or flip-flops. Women: Jeans or trousers with a nice top, simple dress, optional blazer; smart sneakers, ankle boots or flats.

Title: Dress code: Chic – what to wear
Description: On Dutch invitations 'chic' usually means clearly smarter than smart casual, but no tuxedo. Similar to cocktail. Men: Suit, or a nice blazer with trousers, shirt, optional tie, smart leather shoes. Women: Elegant dress, dressy trousers with a blouse or a jumpsuit; heels or smart flats.

Title: Dress code: Jacket required – what to wear
Description: Common at upscale restaurants, clubs and members' clubs: men wear a jacket. 'Jacket and tie' means a tie as well. Title: Dress code: Country attire – what to wear

Description: For religious sites and ceremonies: shoulders and knees covered, nothing sheer or tight. Always follow what the host asks. Men: Long trousers and a shirt with sleeves. Title: Dress code: Nautical – what to wear
Description: Maritime theme or an event on a boat: navy, white, red and stripes. Men: Navy blazer, white or striped shirt, white or beige trousers, boat shoes (soft soles on board). Women: Striped top, white trousers or navy dress, flat shoes (no heels on deck).

Title: Dress code: Funeral attire – what to wear

Title: Dress code: All white – what to wear
Description: Everyone wears white (or off-white). Men: White shirt or polo with white or cream trousers, light shoes. Women: White dress, trousers or jumpsuit. Never white at a wedding unless asked.

Title: Dress code: Roaring twenties – what to wear

Title: Dress code: Tropical – what to wear
Description: Bright and summery, often for garden and theme parties. Men: Hawaiian shirt, linen shorts or trousers. Women: Tropical-print sundress, flowers in your hair.
Keywords: dress code, tropical, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a wedding
Description: Check the invitation first: it often states a dress code. If it doesn't, go semi-formal: smart, festive and suited to the time and venue. A beach wedding calls for something different from a dinner at a castle. Men: A suit and tie is almost always right. In the daytime and outdoors it can be lighter in colour and without a tie; in the evening, go dark. Women: A festive dress or jumpsuit. Don't wear white or cream, or anything that competes with the bride. On grass or sand:…
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a wedding, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a gala
Description: A gala is usually the most formal party of the year. If the invitation states no dress code, assume black tie. School and company galas are sometimes a little less strict, but it's hard to be overdressed here. Men: A tuxedo with a black bow tie. No tuxedo? Then a dark suit with a plain tie and polished shoes. Women: A floor-length evening gown, or an elegant cocktail dress if it's less formal. Finish with jewellery and a clutch.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a gala, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a Christmas party
Description: A Christmas party can be smart and festive: think velvet, sparkle or a cheerful colour. Keep it a little more modest at work than with friends. If the invitation says 'festive', you can really go for it. Men: A blazer or suit, perhaps in velvet or with a cheerful tie, bow tie or pocket square. At a casual party, a nice jumper over a shirt also works. Women: A dress or skirt in sequins, satin or velvet, or smart trousers with a festive top.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a christmas party, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a job interview
Description: Dress one step smarter than the people who already work there. Check the company's website or social media beforehand to see what staff wear. Neat and well-fitting matters more than expensive. Men: For banks, law firms and government: a dark suit and tie. For most other companies: a blazer with chinos or trousers and a shirt, no tie. Women: A trouser suit, or trousers or a skirt with a blouse and blazer. Choose closed shoes and keep jewellery and make-up understated.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a job interview, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to an office party
Description: It's a party, but with your colleagues and managers. Choose something more festive than your work clothes, yet something you'd also dare wear at the office. Always follow the dress code on the invitation: at a theme party, dressing up is appreciated. Men: A blazer with chinos or trousers and a nice shirt. For a smarter party, a suit; a tie is usually not needed. Women: A smart dress, jumpsuit or trousers with a festive top. Avoid anything too short or revealing.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to an office party, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a networking event
Description: You want to look professional yet approachable. Business casual is almost always the safe choice. If people come straight from work, what you wore to the office that day is usually fine. Men: Chinos or trousers with a shirt, optionally a blazer. A tie is only needed in formal industries. Women: Trousers or a skirt with a blouse or fine knit, optionally a blazer. Choose shoes you can stand in for a long time.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a networking event, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to the theatre or opera
Description: For an ordinary performance, smart casual is fine these days. At a premiere, gala night or the opera, many people dress up more, sometimes even in black tie. Check your ticket or the theatre's website for a dress code. Men: Chinos or trousers with a shirt and blazer. For a premiere or opera gala, a dark suit or tuxedo. Women: A smart dress or trousers with a nice top. For a premiere, a cocktail or evening dress is fine.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to the theatre or opera, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a fancy restaurant
Description: Some top restaurants require a jacket ('jacket required'); it's usually stated on their website. At most upscale restaurants, smart casual to cocktail is fine. Leave sportswear, flip-flops and caps at home. Men: A blazer with trousers or dark jeans and a shirt. Where a jacket is required, a sport coat is a must, sometimes a tie too. Women: An elegant dress, or nice trousers with a silk top or blouse.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a fancy restaurant, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear on a first date
Description: Wear something you feel comfortable and yourself in, just a little smarter than usual. Match it to the venue: a walk calls for something different from a cocktail bar. Neat hair, clean shoes and smelling fresh count for more than an expensive brand. Men: Dark jeans or chinos, a well-fitting shirt or fine knit and smart sneakers or loafers. Women: Jeans or trousers with a nice top, or a simple dress. Choose shoes you can walk in.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear on a first date, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear on New Year's Eve
Description: New Year's Eve is the moment for sparkle and shine. At home with friends it's festive-casual; at a club or gala it can be fully glamorous. Going outside at midnight? Bring a warm coat. Men: A dark suit or a blazer with a nice shirt, perhaps with a shiny touch like a velvet jacket or a bow tie. Women: Sequins, metallics or satin: a dress, jumpsuit or top that sparkles. A black dress with statement jewellery works too.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear on new year's eve, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a graduation
Description: A graduation is a festive occasion, but usually not a gala. Smart or smart casual is the norm, for graduates and guests alike. If you're going on stage, choose shoes you can walk in confidently. Men: Chinos or trousers with a shirt, optionally a blazer or suit. A tie is optional. Women: A smart dress, or a skirt or trousers with a blouse. Choose shoes that are easy to walk in.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a graduation, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide

Title: What to wear to a christening or communion
Description: These celebrations usually take place in a church, so dress smartly and modestly. Cover your shoulders and avoid anything too short or sheer. A party often follows; the same outfit works well there. Men: A suit, or a blazer with trousers and a shirt. A tie is smart but not required. Women: A dress or skirt to the knee or longer, with covered shoulders (a cardigan or blazer works too). Avoid white; that's for the child.
Keywords: dress code, what to wear to a christening or communion, what to wear, men's outfit, women's outfit, style guide
